summary: A minimal self-improving ML agent loop: propose experiment → train → evaluate → keep/discard. Ran 700 experiments on one GPU in 2 days, discovering 20 optimizations autonomously. 59k GitHub stars.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the propose/evaluate/keep loop pattern mirrors AgentForge's plan/implement/review cycle; the external-validation insight (run real tests, not model self-critique) is directly applicable. No direct adoption path without rearchitecting the training-specific loop into software orchestration.

summary: CodeAct collapses multi-step tool-call chains into a single model-generated Python program executed in a Hyperlight micro-VM. Reduces agent latency ~50% and token usage ~60% vs. sequential tool calls.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge agents are CLI subprocesses (claude, codex) communicating via stdin/stdout, not API-based tool-calling agents. CodeAct requires a Python sandbox runtime and tool API surface that AgentForge does not have. Architecturally incompatible in 1-2 runs.

source: LangMem — LangGraph cross-run episodic and semantic memory
summary: LangMem adds cross-session episodic, semantic, and procedural memory to LangGraph agents via a PostgresStore. Production pattern: pair LangGraph PostgresSaver (thread checkpointing) with Mem0/Letta for facts that survive across sessions.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly maps to the cross-run episodic memory gap. However, this capability is already tracked by open issue HID-188 (inject cross-run episodic memory into planner and executor prompts).

source: Self-Improving AI Agents: Reflection Loops 2026 survey (Turing Post + arXiv 2607.24300)
summary: Survey of self-improving agent loop patterns. Key finding: LLMs cannot reliably self-correct without external feedback; the strongest reflection systems run real checks (execute tests, check metrics). Recommends capping reflection loops at 2-3 iterations.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the 'run real tests as external signal' insight supports HID-135 (synthesize acceptance test harness from plan). The retry/reflection loop themes overlap with HID-186 (stage-level partial retry) and HID-167 (automatic retry with failure classification). All themes already tracked.

summary: Intent-to-contract synthesis harness for AI coding agents: converts a structured plan into a set of acceptance contracts (tests) that gate execution and completion. Released August 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — strongly supports HID-135 (synthesize acceptance test harness from approved plan before implementation). No new issue warranted; strengthens the existing issue's design.

summary: Karpathy's 'agentic engineering' term (Feb 2026): humans define specs/boundaries; models iterate, generate, and reconcile. 9-rule architecture: models handle execution bookkeeping, humans maintain oversight and spec. Emphasis on single-feature iteration loops.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — philosophical alignment with AgentForge's design (human approves plan, agents implement). No new capability gap identified; consistent with existing architecture.

source: ZenBrain: 7-Layer Memory Architecture for Autonomous AI (arXiv 2604.23878)
summary: Neuroscience-inspired 7-layer memory model for AI agents: sensory buffer, working memory, episodic, semantic, procedural, prospective, and meta-memory layers. Proposes Fibonacci-weighted retrieval across layers.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — complex multi-layer memory architecture would require substantial new infrastructure. AgentForge's memory model (skill distillation + episodic tracked in HID-188) is simpler and more suitable for the current stage.

source: How Do Agent Harnesses Create Value? (arXiv 2609.20474)
summary: Empirical study on how planning information and release controls in agent harnesses affect task success, erroneous acceptance, and cost. Finds structured planning + verification gates reduce false completions by 40%.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — supports policyEngine.ts design and HID-93 (adversarial plan critique). The release control findings strengthen the case for HID-135. No new gap identified.
